description: Design a simple Kalman filter module in Verilog that fuses position data from a noisy sensor. Design a Verilog module for a simple RC oscillator that produces a square wave output. The oscillator should toggle its output state based on a clock signal and a control signal that simulates the RC charging and discharging behavior. The output frequency should be determined by the control signal. The module should also include a reset signal to initialize the output state.
code:
module RC_Oscillator(
    input wire clk,      // Clock input
    input wire reset,    // Asynchronous reset
    input wire control,  // Control signal to determine the frequency
    output reg out       // Square wave output
);
    reg [23:0] counter;  // 24-bit counter for frequency division

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            out <= 0;
            counter <= 0;
        end else begin
            if (counter < (control ? 24'd999999 : 24'd499999)) begin
                counter <= counter + 1;
            end else begin
                counter <= 0;
                out <= ~out; // Toggle output
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

Design a 4-bit Parallel-in Serial-out (PISO) shift register in Verilog. The PISO shift register should allow loading a 4-bit parallel input when a load signal is active, and it should shift out one bit at a time on every clock pulse when not loading. The output should be available on a serial output line.
code:
module PISO (
    input wire clk,
    input wire load,
    input wire [3:0] parallel_in,
    output reg serial_out
);
    reg [3:0] shift_reg;
    reg [2:0] count;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (load) begin
            shift_reg <= parallel_in; // Load parallel data
            count <= 3'b100; // Set count to 4 (for 4 bits)
        end else if (count > 0) begin
            serial_out <= shift_reg[3]; // Output the most significant bit
            shift_reg <= shift_reg << 1; // Shift left
            count <= count - 1; // Decrement the count
        end
    end
endmodule

Design a data forwarding unit for a simple 5-stage pipeline processor. The forwarding unit should take three inputs: the destination register of the instruction in the EX stage, the destination register of the instruction in the MEM stage, and the destination register of the instruction in the WB stage. It should output two signals: ForwardA and ForwardB, which indicate whether the data should be forwarded from the EX or MEM stages for the first and second operands, respectively.

module data_forwarding_unit(

    input [4:0] MEM_dest,  
    input [4:0] WB_dest,  
    input EX_valid,  
    input MEM_valid,  
    input WB_valid,  
    output reg ForwardA,  
    output reg ForwardB  
);  
    always @(*) begin  
        ForwardA = 0;  
        ForwardB = 0;  
        
        if (EX_valid && (EX_dest != 0)) begin  
            ForwardA = (EX_dest == WB_dest) ? 1 : ForwardA;  
        end  
        
        if (MEM_valid && (MEM_dest != 0)) begin  
            ForwardA = (MEM_dest == WB_dest) ? 1 : ForwardA;  
        end  
        
        if (EX_valid && (EX_dest != 0)) begin  
            ForwardB = (EX_dest == MEM_dest) ? 1 : ForwardB;  
        end  
        
        if (MEM_valid && (MEM_dest != 0)) begin  
            ForwardB = (MEM_dest == WB_dest) ? 1 : ForwardB;

endmodule

Design a SPI master controller that can communicate with a SPI slave device. The SPI master should support the following operations: sending data to the slave, receiving data from the slave, and handling the clock signal. The controller should have an enable signal and a 8-bit data input for sending data. The output should be an 8-bit data received from the slave. The clock should toggle as per the SPI protocol, and the data should be shifted out and in on the rising edge of the clock.
code:
module spi_master (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire enable,
    input wire [7:0] data_in,
    output reg [7:0] data_out,
    output reg sclk,
    output reg mosi,
    input wire miso
);
    reg [3:0] bit_index;
    reg [7:0] shift_reg;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            bit_index <= 0;
            sclk <= 0;
            mosi <= 0;
            data_out <= 0;
            shift_reg <= 0;
        end else if (enable) begin
            if (bit_index < 8) begin
                sclk <= ~sclk; // Toggle clock
                if (sclk) begin
                    mosi <= data_in[7 - bit_index]; // Send bit
                end else begin
                    shift_reg[7 - bit_index] <= miso; // Receive bit
                    bit_index <= bit_index + 1;
                end
            end else begin
                data_out <= shift_reg; // Complete transfer
                bit_index <= 0; // Reset for next transfer
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

The counter should increment when a branch is taken and decrement when it is not taken, with limits to keep the counter within 0 and 3. The system should output whether the branch was predicted to be taken or not taken based on the counter value.
code:
module branch_predictor (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input branch_outcome, // 1 for taken, 0 for not taken
    output reg prediction // 1 for taken, 0 for not taken
);
    reg [1:0] state; // 00: Strongly Not Taken, 01: Weakly Not Taken, 10: Weakly Taken, 11: Strongly Taken

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= 2'b00; // Start in Strongly Not Taken state
            prediction <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                2'b00: begin // Strongly Not Taken
                    if (branch_outcome) begin
                        state <= 2'b01; // Move to Weakly Not Taken
                        prediction <= 0; // Predict Not Taken
                    end else begin
                        prediction <= 0; // Predict Not Taken
                    end
                end
                2'b01: begin // Weakly Not Taken
                    if (branch_outcome) begin
                        state <= 2'b10; // Move to Weakly Taken
                        prediction <= 0; // Predict Not Taken
                    end else begin
                        state <= 2'b00; // Move to Strongly Not Taken
                        prediction <= 0; // Predict Not Taken
                    end
                end
                2'b10: begin // Weakly Taken
                    if (branch_outcome) begin
                        state <= 2'b11; // Move to Strongly Taken
                        prediction <= 1; // Predict Taken
                    end else begin
                        state <= 2'b01; // Move to Weakly Not Taken
                        prediction <= 1; // Predict Taken
                    end
                end
                2'b11: begin // Strongly Taken
                    if (branch_outcome) begin
                        prediction <= 1; // Predict Taken
                    end else begin
                        state <= 2'b10; // Move to Weakly Taken
                        prediction <= 1; // Predict Taken
                    end
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

- If Clear is high, the output Q should be reset to 0.
- On the rising edge of the Clock, if J and K are both low, the output Q should remain unchanged.
- If J is high and K is low, Q should be set to 1.
- If J is low and K is high, Q should be set to 0.
- If both J and K are high, Q should toggle its state.

    input wire J,
    input wire K,
    input wire clk,
    input wire clear,
    output reg Q
);
    always @(posedge clk or posedge clear) begin
        if (clear) begin
            Q <= 0;
        end else begin
            case ({J, K})
                2'b00: Q <= Q;      // No change
                2'b10: Q <= 1;      // Set
                2'b01: Q <= 0;      // Reset
                2'b11: Q <= ~Q;     // Toggle

    end
endmodule

description: Design a simple Verilog module that implements a Depth-First Search (DFS) traversal for a binary tree. The module should accept a binary tree as input and provide the DFS output as a series of values emitted in order. The tree structure will be defined using a set of register values representing node values. The traversal should be initiated by a start signal.
code:
module DFS_BinaryTree (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire start,
    input wire [7:0] node_value,
    output reg [7:0] dfs_output,
    output reg done
);
    reg [3:0] state;
    reg [15:0] stack [0:15]; // Stack for DFS
    reg [3:0] sp; // Stack pointer

    parameter IDLE = 0, PUSH = 1, POP = 2, OUTPUT = 3;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= IDLE;
            sp <= 0;
            done <= 0;
            dfs_output <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (start) begin
                        stack[sp] <= node_value; // Push the root node
                        sp <= sp + 1;
                        state <= PUSH;
                    end
                end
                PUSH: begin
                    if (sp > 0) begin
                        dfs_output <= stack[sp - 1]; // Output the top of the stack
                        sp <= sp - 1; // Pop the stack
                        state <= OUTPUT;
                    end else begin
                        done <= 1; // No more nodes to process
                        state <= IDLE; // Go back to IDLE
                    end
                end
                OUTPUT: begin
                    state <= PUSH; // Go back to pushing next node
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a Watchdog Timer in Verilog. The timer should have an input signal `reset` (active high), an input signal `feed` (active high), and an output signal `timeout`. The timer should timeout after a certain period unless it is fed within that period. The period can be simulated using a counter. When `reset` is high, the timer should reset. When `feed` is high, the timer should restart its counting. The output `timeout` should be high if the timer reaches the maximum count without being fed.

module watchdog_timer(
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire feed,
    output reg timeout
);

    parameter MAX_COUNT = 10; // Define the maximum count for timeout
    reg [3:0] count; // 4-bit counter

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            count <= 0;
            timeout <= 0;
        end else if (feed) begin
            count <= 0; // Reset count on feed
            timeout <= 0; // Reset timeout
        end else begin
            if (count >= MAX_COUNT) begin
                timeout <= 1; // Set timeout if max count reached
            end else begin
                count <= count + 1; // Increment the counter
                timeout <= 0; // Ensure timeout is low until max count
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

            case (state)  
                2'b00: begin // strongly not taken  
                    if (branch_signal) begin  
                        state <= 2'b01; // go to weakly taken  
                    end  
                    prediction <= 0;  
                end  
                2'b01: begin // weakly taken

                    end else begin  
                        state <= 2'b01; // go to weakly taken  
                    end  
                    prediction <= 1;  
                end  
                2'b11: begin // strongly taken  
                    if (branch_signal) begin  
                        state <= 2'b11; // stay in strongly taken

The module should take the number of vertices, the weight matrix, and an initial source vertex as inputs, and output the shortest distances from the source to all other vertices.

module bellman_ford #(parameter N = 5) (  
    input [N*N-1:0] weights, // NxN weight matrix flattened  
    input [2:0] source,      // source vertex (0 to N-1)  
    output reg [N*8-1:0] distances // distances array (8 bits for each vertex)  
);  
    integer i, j, k;  
    reg [7:0] dist [0:N-1];  

    always @(*) begin  
        // Initialize distances  
        for (i = 0; i < N; i = i + 1) begin  
            dist[i] = 8'hFF; // Set to infinity  
        end  
        dist[source] = 8'h00; // Distance to self is 0  

        // Relax edges up to N-1 times  
        for (k = 0; k < N-1; k = k + 1) begin  
            for (i = 0; i < N; i = i + 1) begin  
                for (j = 0; j < N; j = j + 1) begin  
                    if (weights[i*N+j] != 8'hFF && dist[i] != 8'hFF) begin  
                        if (dist[i] + weights[i*N+j] < dist[j]) begin  
                            dist[j] = dist[i] + weights[i*N+j];  
                        end  
                    end  
                end  
            end  
        end  

        // Pack distances into output  
        for (i = 0; i < N; i = i + 1) begin  
            distances[i*8 +: 8] = dist[i];  
        end  
    end  
endmodule

You should handle division by zero gracefully, setting the quotient to 0 and the remainder to the dividend in that case.

module non_restoring_divider (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input [7:0] dividend,
    input [7:0] divisor,
    input start,
    output reg [15:0] quotient,
    output reg [7:0] remainder,
    output reg done
);

    reg [15:0] A; // Accumulator
    reg [7:0] B; // Divisor
    reg [4:0] count;
    reg state; // 0: idle, 1: busy

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            A <= 0;
            B <= 0;
            count <= 0;
            quotient <= 0;
            remainder <= 0;
            done <= 0;
            state <= 0;
        end else if (start && state == 0) begin
            // Initialize A and B
            A <= {8'b0, dividend}; // Load dividend
            B <= divisor;          // Load divisor
            quotient <= 0;        // Clear quotient
            remainder <= 0;       // Clear remainder
            count <= 8;          // Set count for 8 bits
            state <= 1;          // Set state to busy
            done <= 0;
        end else if (state == 1) begin
            if (count > 0) begin
                A <= {A[14:0], 1'b0}; // Shift A left
                if (A[15:8] >= B) begin
                    A <= A - {B, 8'b0}; // Subtract B
                    quotient <= {quotient[14:0], 1'b1}; // Append 1 to quotient
                end else begin
                    quotient <= {quotient[14:0], 1'b0}; // Append 0 to quotient
                end
                count <= count - 1; // Decrement count
            end else begin
                remainder <= A[7:0]; // Remainder is the last 8 bits of A
                state <= 0;          // Set state back to idle
                done <= 1;           // Indicate done
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a fixed-priority arbiter that selects one of several requests based on a predefined priority. module fixed_priority_arbiter (

    input wire rst_n,
    input wire enable,
    input wire [4:0] req,
    output reg [4:0] gnt
);
    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            gnt <= 5'b00000;
        end else if (enable) begin
            gnt <= 5'b00000; // Default to no grant
            if (req[0]) gnt[0] <= 1'b1; // Grant req0
            else if (req[1]) gnt[1] <= 1'b1; // Grant req1
            else if (req[2]) gnt[2] <= 1'b1; // Grant req2

    end
endmodule

The output should be a clock signal that locks onto the input reference clock. Implement a simple counter as the VCO that increments based on the phase detection result.

Create a pulse generator that produces a single pulse of a specified width and period. The pulse width and period can be set by input parameters, and the pulse should be active high. The system should also have a reset input that initializes the generator.

);

description: Design a UART transmitter that takes an 8-bit data input, a start bit, and a stop bit. The transmitter should shift out the bits serially, including the start bit at the beginning, followed by the data bits (LSB first), and the stop bit at the end. The output should be available on a single serial line. You need to provide a clock signal that controls the timing of the data output.
code:
module uart_transmitter (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire start,
    input wire [7:0] data_in,
    output reg tx,
    output reg ready
);
    reg [3:0] bit_index; // To track the current bit position
    reg [10:0] shift_reg; // 1 start + 8 data + 1 stop = 10 bits
    reg sending; // Flag to indicate if we are currently sending data

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            tx <= 1; // Idle state (high)
            ready <= 1; // Ready to send new data
            sending <= 0;
            bit_index <= 0;
        end else if (start && ready) begin
            shift_reg <= {1'b1, data_in, 1'b0}; // Load the shift register with stop bit and data
            tx <= 0; // Start bit
            sending <= 1; // Set sending flag
            bit_index <= 0; // Start from the first bit
            ready <= 0; // Not ready until done
        end else if (sending) begin
            if (bit_index < 10) begin
                tx <= shift_reg[bit_index]; // Shift out the next bit
                bit_index <= bit_index + 1; // Move to the next bit
            end else begin
                sending <= 0; // Finished sending
                tx <= 1; // Set tx back to idle state
                ready <= 1; // Ready to send new data
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

description:
You are to implement a simple Direct Memory Access (DMA) controller in Verilog. The DMA controller should be able to transfer data from a source memory address to a destination memory address. It will have the following inputs:
- `clk`: Clock signal
- `start`: Signal to start the DMA transfer
- `src_addr`: Source memory address (8 bits)
- `dst_addr`: Destination memory address (8 bits)
- `data_in`: Data input from memory (8 bits)
- `ack`: Acknowledge signal from the destination memory

And the outputs:
- `data_out`: Data output to the destination memory (8 bits)
- `done`: Signal indicating the DMA transfer is complete

The controller should transfer 8 bytes of data, incrementing the source and destination addresses after each byte is transferred. The `done` signal should be asserted after the last byte is transferred.

module dma_controller (
    input wire clk,
    input wire start,
    input wire [7:0] src_addr,
    input wire [7:0] dst_addr,
    input wire [7:0] data_in,
    input wire ack,
    output reg [7:0] data_out,
    output reg done
);
    reg [7:0] src_addr_reg;
    reg [7:0] dst_addr_reg;
    reg [2:0] byte_count; // counts bytes transferred

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (start) begin
            src_addr_reg <= src_addr;
            dst_addr_reg <= dst_addr;
            byte_count <= 3'b0;
            done <= 1'b0;
        end else if (byte_count < 3'd8) begin
            if (ack) begin // wait for ack signal
                data_out <= data_in; // transfer data
                src_addr_reg <= src_addr_reg + 1; // increment src
                dst_addr_reg <= dst_addr_reg + 1; // increment dst
                byte_count <= byte_count + 1; // increment byte count
            end
        end else begin
            done <= 1'b1; // signal done after 8 bytes
        end
    end
endmodule

    output reg sclk,

    output reg [7:0] data_out
);

    reg [7:0] shift_reg;
    reg state; // 0: idle, 1: sending
    
    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            sclk <= 0;
            ss <= 1;
            bit_cnt <= 0;
            shift_reg <= 0;
            data_out <= 0;
            state <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                0: begin // Idle State
                    ss <= 1;
                    if (start) begin
                        ss <= 0; // Enable slave
                        shift_reg <= data_in; // Load data
                        bit_cnt <= 0;
                        state <= 1; // Move to sending state
                    end
                end
                1: begin // Sending State
                    sclk <= ~sclk; // Generate clock
                    if (sclk) begin // On rising edge
                        data_out[bit_cnt] <= mosi; // Read data
                        shift_reg <= {shift_reg[6:0], 1'b0}; // Shift left
                        bit_cnt <= bit_cnt + 1;
                        if (bit_cnt == 7) begin
                            state <= 0; // Go back to idle
                        end

            endcase

    end

    input rst,
    input [15:0] noisy_measurement,
    output reg [15:0] filtered_value
);

    parameter R = 16'h0004; // measurement noise covariance

    reg [15:0] k; // Kalman gain

        if (rst) begin
            x <= 16'h0000;
            p <= 16'h0001; // initial estimation error covariance
            filtered_value <= 16'h0000;
        end else begin

            p <= p + Q; 

            // Measurement update
            k <= p / (p + R); // Compute Kalman gain
            x <= x + k * (noisy_measurement - x); // Update state estimate

    end
endmodule

description: Design a digital phase shifter that takes a clock signal and an input signal, and outputs a phase-shifted version of the input signal. The phase shift should be configurable via a 2-bit control signal. The control signal will determine the amount of phase shift: 00 for 0 degrees, 01 for 90 degrees, 10 for 180 degrees, and 11 for 270 degrees. The output should be sampled on the rising edge of the clock.
code:
module phase_shifter (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire [1:0] phase_ctrl,
    input wire in_signal,
    output reg out_signal
);
    reg [1:0] state;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            state <= 2'b00;
            out_signal <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            state <= phase_ctrl;
            case (state)
                2'b00: out_signal <= in_signal;       // 0 degrees
                2'b01: out_signal <= in_signal ^ 1'b1; // 90 degrees (Inverted)
                2'b10: out_signal <= in_signal;        // 180 degrees (Same signal)
                2'b11: out_signal <= in_signal ^ 1'b1; // 270 degrees (Inverted)
                default: out_signal <= in_signal;
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

);

description:
Design a 4-bit SRAM cell that allows for reading and writing data. The SRAM cell should have the following inputs and outputs:
- Inputs:

  - we (write enable signal),
  - data_in (4-bit input data),
  - addr (2-bit address input to select the SRAM cell).
- Outputs:
  - data_out (4-bit output data).
When `we` is high, the data from `data_in` should be written to the memory location specified by `addr`. When `we` is low, the data from the memory location specified by `addr` should be output on `data_out`.
code:
module SRAM_4bit (
    input wire clk,
    input wire we,
    input wire [3:0] data_in,
    input wire [1:0] addr,
    output reg [3:0] data_out
);
    reg [3:0] memory [0:3]; // 4-bit SRAM with 4 addresses
    
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (we) begin
            memory[addr] <= data_in; // Write data to SRAM
        end
        else begin
            data_out <= memory[addr]; // Read data from SRAM
        end
    end
endmodule

description:
Design a fan speed controller based on temperature input. The fan can have three speed settings: low, medium, and high. The speed is determined by a 2-bit input temperature signal. The mapping is as follows: 
00 -> Off
01 -> Low
10 -> Medium
11 -> High

code:

    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire [1:0] temperature,
    output reg [1:0] fan_speed
);

    if (rst) begin
        fan_speed <= 2'b00; // Off
    end else begin
        case (temperature)
            2'b00: fan_speed <= 2'b00; // Off
            2'b01: fan_speed <= 2'b01; // Low
            2'b10: fan_speed <= 2'b10; // Medium
            2'b11: fan_speed <= 2'b11; // High
            default: fan_speed <= 2'b00; // Default to Off
        endcase
    end
end

endmodule

Design a restoring divider that takes a 4-bit dividend and a 4-bit divisor as inputs and produces a 4-bit quotient and a 4-bit remainder. The division should be performed using the restoring division algorithm. The division process should be clocked and should handle resets.
code:
module restoring_divider (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input [3:0] dividend,
    input [3:0] divisor,
    output reg [3:0] quotient,
    output reg [3:0] remainder,
    output reg done
);
    reg [3:0] A; // Accumulator
    reg [3:0] Q; // Quotient
    reg [3:0] M; // Divisor
    reg [3:0] count; // Count for iterations
    reg state; // State to indicate processing

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            A <= 4'b0000;
            Q <= 4'b0000;
            M <= divisor;
            quotient <= 4'b0000;
            remainder <= 4'b0000;
            done <= 0;
            count <= 4; // Number of bits for division
            state <= 1; // Start state
        end else if (state) begin
            if (count > 0) begin
                A <= {A[2:0], Q[3]}; // Shift left
                Q <= {Q[2:0], 1'b0}; // Shift left in Q
                A <= A - M; // Subtract divisor from A

                if (A[3] == 1) begin // A < 0
                    A <= A + M; // Restore A
                    Q[0] <= 0; // No change in Q
                end else begin
                    Q[0] <= 1; // Set Q bit
                end
                count <= count - 1; // Decrement count
            end else begin
                quotient <= Q;
                remainder <= A;
                done <= 1; // Indicate division is done
                state <= 0; // End state
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

A SR flip-flop is required that responds to set (S) and reset (R) inputs. The flip-flop should also have a clock (CLK) input that triggers the output (Q) on the rising edge of the clock. If both S and R are high, the output should remain in its previous state (not allowed condition).
code:
module sr_flip_flop (
    input wire S,
    input wire R,
    input wire CLK,
    output reg Q,
    output reg Qn
);
    always @(posedge CLK) begin
        if (S && R) begin
            // Do nothing to maintain the previous state
            Q <= Q; // Hold state
        end else if (S) begin
            Q <= 1'b1; // Set
        end else if (R) begin
            Q <= 1'b0; // Reset
        end
        Qn <= ~Q; // Complement output
    end
endmodule

);

description: Design a D-flip-flop module in Verilog. The D-flip-flop should have a clock input (clk), a reset input (rst), a data input (D), and a data output (Q). When the reset is asserted, the output Q should be set to 0. On the rising edge of the clock, the output Q should take the value of D.

Design a 16-bit Linear Feedback Shift Register (LFSR) in Verilog. The LFSR should have an initial seed value loaded with a parallel load signal and should shift on every clock cycle. The feedback polynomial to be used is defined as x^16 + x^14 + x^13 + x^11 + 1. Implement a module that outputs the current value of the LFSR after each clock cycle.
code:
module LFSR (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input load,
    input [15:0] seed,
    output reg [15:0] lfsr_out
);
    wire feedback;

    // Feedback polynomial: x^16 + x^14 + x^13 + x^11 + 1
    assign feedback = lfsr_out[15] ^ lfsr_out[13] ^ lfsr_out[12] ^ lfsr_out[10];

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            lfsr_out <= 16'h1; // Default seed
        end else if (load) begin
            lfsr_out <= seed; // Load new seed
        end else begin
            lfsr_out <= {lfsr_out[14:0], feedback}; // Shift and insert feedback
        end
    end
endmodule
